notes:
Source Hunter pairs a Chrome extension with a local workbench. Highlight a public-page claim, inspect its source trail and exact wording, distinguish publication/measurement/capture dates, and export the investigation.

TinyResearch proposes a trail; TinyFish Fetch checks exact pages and observed links. Proposed attribution, independently found comparisons and failed retrievals remain separate. Missing originals stay unresolved.

The 2:04 video shows five real recorded claims across public health, cybersecurity, astronomy and historical writing. WHO’s food-security estimate has a supported rounding explanation. NASA contradicts the historical unaided Great Wall Moon-visibility assertion; the selected article examines that myth rather than endorsing it.

A separate unseen NOAA selection was tested through the installed Chrome extension. One Deep job and nine checks completed after manual same-receipt recovery; a separately authorized tenth PDF check reached the NOAA/NASA producer briefing. The original export is preserved. Its earliest origin, exact publication day, underlying dataset validation and portal-to-PDF citation edge remain unproved.

Public repo/setup: https://github.com/himanshu748/source-hunter
The recorded preview runs locally without credentials. Fresh research needs the operator’s own TinyFish access, explicit pricing/tier checks and bounded grant; it is paused in the review build. Anonymous clean setup, 99 tests, types/build/review/format, and actual Chrome/workbench checks passed. Mobile sizing and OS reduced-motion emulation remain unverified; CSV extraction is mock-tested only.
